newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, led by gold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Tuesday, as the complex drifted lower for the fourth day in a row.
"Gold came under extra pressure late in the day on more news about the IMF gold sale," Credit Lyonnais Rouse's New York chief bullion dealer, Scott Mehlman said.
"The $378 level (basis December) is under pressure again, but hasn't broken yet and as the market is already heavily short, a covering rally wouldn't be a surprise either."
COMEX December gold closed down $1.30 an ounce at $378.40, after seeing a session low at $378.20.
December gold saw life-of-contract lows at $377.70 on October 31.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $377.85/378.35, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $378.20 and the New York close Monday around $378.80/379.30.
Spot gold has also found support twice since early October around $377.00 an ounce, and now looks stuck in a $377.00-385.00 range, traders said.

Late in the day, IMF treasurer David Williams told a London conference that, if the proposed IMF gold sale of five million ounces goes ahead, about 500,000 ounces would be sold at a time, amounting to about seven percent of daily market turnover.
The total sale of five million ounces would amount to about five percent of annual gold supply, eight percent of annual gold mine output and 60 percent of daily market turnover.

However, he stressed the sale was unlikely to take place in 1997 and would only occur if the IMF and its member countries did not meet the financing requirements of the Enhance Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) from member contributions or further borrowing
The ESAF is designed to relieve the debt burden of 20 of the world's poorest countries.
Earlier the IMF sold 50 million ounces of gold between 1976 and 1980.
Other bearish fundamentals are hanging over the market also, traders said.
Asian demand has been lower in 1996 than last year, due to the strength of the U.S. dollar, and year-end producer hedging has been noted recently.
COMEX December silver ended down 1.0 cent at $4.873 an ounce, after trading in a $4.885-4.855 range.
While some support for spot silver has developed around $4.85 an ounce, the long term downtrend since February remains intact, providing resistance on any rebound toward $5.00, analysts said.
NYMEX January platinum closed down $2.30 at $387.00 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium ended down 25 cents at $119.00 an ounce.
-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1640; email: clive.mckeef@reuter.com
